q: The assurance obtained in a review of interim financial information under SRE 2410 is:
o: Reasonable assurance, expressed in the positive form of words
Limited assurance, the conclusion expressed in negative form
Absolute assurance on the interim figures taken as a whole
No assurance, the work being an agreed-upon procedures job
why: A review engagement provides limited assurance and the conclusion is expressed in negative form, stating that nothing has come to the auditor attention that causes the auditor to believe the interim financial information is not prepared in accordance with the applicable framework. Reasonable assurance and positive expression belong to an audit.

q: Under SRE 2410, the procedures in a review of interim financial information ordinarily consist of:
o: Tests of controls and substantive tests of details of balances
Inquiry of finance staff and analytical and other review procedures
Physical verification of inventory and external confirmation of receivables
Full substantive procedures applied at a reduced sample size
why: SRE 2410 describes review procedures as ordinarily limited to making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. Tests of controls, confirmations and physical verification are audit procedures and are not ordinarily performed.

q: Under SRE 2410, the practitioner performing the review of interim financial information is presumed to:
o: Be a firm other than the statutory auditor, to ensure independence
Be the auditor of the entity annual financial statements
Be appointed by the audit committee for each quarter separately
Have no prior knowledge of the entity or of its internal control
why: SRE 2410 deals with a review of interim financial information performed by the independent auditor of the entity, and the standard assumes the reviewer has an understanding of the entity and its internal control obtained through the annual audit. A reviewer without such knowledge would follow a different standard.

q: During a limited review, the auditor becomes aware of a matter that causes belief that a material misstatement exists. The auditor should:
o: Issue a disclaimer of conclusion on the interim information at once
Make additional inquiries or perform other procedures to conclude on it
Convert the engagement into a statutory audit of the interim figures
Report the matter to SEBI before the review is completed and issued
why: SRE 2410 requires that if a matter comes to the auditor attention that causes belief that the interim financial information may be materially misstated, the auditor should make additional inquiries or perform other procedures sufficient to enable the expression of a conclusion. Escalation of procedures precedes any modification of the conclusion.

q: Under SEBI LODR Regulation 33, a listed entity must submit quarterly and year-to-date standalone financial results within:
o: 30 days from the end of the quarter, other than the last quarter
45 days from the end of the quarter, other than the last quarter
60 days from the end of the quarter, other than the last quarter
45 days from the end of every quarter, including the last quarter
why: Quarterly and year-to-date results must be submitted within forty five days of the end of each quarter other than the last quarter. For the last quarter and the year, audited annual results are submitted within sixty days from the end of the financial year.

q: A listed entity submits audited annual financial results for the financial year. Under SEBI LODR Regulation 33, the timeline is:
o: Within 60 days from the end of the relevant financial year of the entity
Within 45 days from the end of the financial year, as for quarters
Within 90 days from the end of the financial year of the entity
Within 30 days from the date of the annual general meeting held
why: Audited results for the full financial year must be submitted within sixty days from the end of the financial year, together with the audit report and a declaration on unmodified opinion where applicable. The forty five day timeline applies to the quarterly results other than the last quarter.

q: A listed entity chooses to submit audited financial results for the last quarter instead of unaudited results with a limited review report. Under SEBI LODR this is:
o: Permitted, along with the annual audited results for the year
Not permitted, the last quarter results always being reviewed
Permitted only with the prior approval of the stock exchange
Permitted only above a prescribed market capitalisation level
why: The regulation allows a listed entity to submit unaudited results for the last quarter with a limited review report, or alternatively to submit audited results for the last quarter along with the annual audited results. There is no exchange approval or market capitalisation condition.

q: Where a listed entity has subsidiaries, SEBI LODR requires the limited review or audit of quarterly consolidated results to cover subsidiaries that account for:
o: At least 60 percent each of the consolidated revenue, assets and profits
All subsidiaries without exception, whatever their size may be
At least 80 percent each of consolidated revenue, assets and profits
Only those subsidiaries that are themselves listed on an exchange
why: The limited review or audit reports submitted on a consolidated basis must cover those subsidiaries that in aggregate account for at least eighty percent of each of consolidated revenue, assets and profits respectively. Sixty percent is a near-miss figure not used in the regulation.

q: If a listed entity submits unaudited quarterly financial results, SEBI LODR requires that they be accompanied by:
o: A limited review report from the statutory auditor of the entity
A certificate from the chief financial officer of the entity only
A management representation letter filed with the stock exchange
An audit report from any firm of accountants the entity chooses
why: Unaudited quarterly and year-to-date results must be accompanied by a limited review report from the statutory auditor of the listed entity. A CFO certification is a separate requirement and cannot substitute for the review report.

q: The conclusion in an unmodified limited review report under SRE 2410 states that:
o: The interim financial information gives a true and fair view of the results
The interim financial information is free from material misstatement
Nothing has come to our attention causing belief of material non-compliance
In our opinion the interim information is fairly presented in all respects
why: The negative form of conclusion is the defining feature of a review report. A statement that the information gives a true and fair view or is fairly presented is the positive expression used in an audit opinion and would overstate the assurance obtained.

q: During a limited review the auditor concludes that a material misstatement exists in the interim financial information, but the effect is not pervasive. The appropriate report is:
o: A qualified conclusion, the matter set out in a preceding paragraph
An adverse conclusion, the misstatement being material to the results
A disclaimer of conclusion, the auditor withholding any conclusion
An unmodified conclusion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph added
why: SRE 2410 requires a qualified conclusion where a material misstatement exists whose effect is not pervasive, with the matter described in a paragraph preceding the conclusion. An adverse conclusion is reserved for effects that are material and pervasive.

q: In a limited review, the auditor is unable to complete the review because management imposes a scope limitation whose possible effects are material and pervasive. The auditor should:
o: Issue a qualified conclusion describing the scope limitation imposed
Issue an adverse conclusion describing the scope limitation imposed
Give no conclusion and inform those charged with governance
Convert the review into an audit and issue an audit opinion instead
why: SRE 2410 provides that when management imposes a limitation that prevents the auditor from completing the review, the auditor should not provide a conclusion and should communicate in writing to those charged with governance the reason why the review cannot be completed, considering whether issuing a report remains appropriate.

q: A key difference between a limited review and an audit of interim financial information is that in a review the auditor:
o: Is not required to be independent of the entity under the Code
Does not obtain an understanding of the entity and its environment
Need not test control effectiveness or obtain external confirmations
Is not required to consider events occurring after the interim date
why: A review does not ordinarily involve testing operating effectiveness of controls, external confirmations, physical inspection or observation, which is why only limited assurance results. Independence, an understanding of the entity and consideration of subsequent events remain necessary in a review.

q: Under SRE 2410, if the auditor identifies a matter causing doubt about whether a material adjustment is needed for the interim information to be in accordance with the framework, and management refuses to adjust, the auditor should:
o: Withdraw from the engagement immediately in every such case
Report the matter only in the annual audit report of the year
Modify the conclusion, inform governance and consider withdrawal
Issue an unmodified conclusion with an explanatory paragraph added
why: Where management does not correct a matter that would make the interim information materially misstated, the auditor modifies the conclusion, communicates the matter to those charged with governance and if the matter is not resolved considers whether to withdraw from the engagement or resign from the appointment as auditor.

q: Under SEBI LODR, the requirement to obtain a limited review report on quarterly results applies to:
o: Only entities ranked in the top 500 by market capitalisation
Only entities that have one or more subsidiary companies
Only entities whose paid-up capital exceeds Rs 10 crore
All listed entities filing unaudited quarterly financial results
why: Regulation 33 applies to listed entities with specified securities and requires that unaudited quarterly and year-to-date results be subjected to a limited review by the statutory auditor. It is not confined to any market capitalisation ranking or capital size.

q: A limited review report on quarterly results is issued by:
o: Any chartered accountant in practice appointed by the board of directors
A peer reviewed firm other than the statutory auditor of the entity
The internal auditor, since the review is not a statutory audit
The statutory auditor, or as specified for public sector entities
why: SEBI LODR requires the limited review to be carried out by the statutory auditor of the listed entity, with a specific accommodation for certain public sector entities where the auditor may be appointed in the prescribed manner. Engaging a different firm or the internal auditor would not satisfy the regulation.

q: Materiality in planning and performing a review of interim financial information under SRE 2410 is determined:
o: At a lower level than annual audit materiality, the period being shorter
Only after the review procedures for the period have been completed
At the same absolute amount as the annual audit materiality always
For the interim information, given the greater risk of non-detection
why: The auditor determines materiality in relation to the interim financial information being reviewed, applying professional judgement while recognising that because review procedures are less extensive there is a greater risk that misstatements will not be detected. Materiality is set during planning, not afterwards.

q: Under SEBI LODR, where a limited review or audit report on financial results contains a modification, the listed entity must:
o: Withhold the results until the modification has been resolved
Restate the results of the preceding four quarters of the financial year
Obtain a second opinion from another auditor before filing it
Disclose the impact and file a statement on impact with the results
why: The regulation requires a listed entity to disclose the cumulative impact of audit qualifications or modifications and file a statement on impact of audit qualifications along with the annual audited results. Results cannot be withheld beyond the prescribed timeline on account of a modification.
